--- title: "The Multiverse" subtitle: "Every line is a justifiable analysis" engine: knitr format: live-html: toc: true webr: packages: - ggplot2 - ggiraph resources: - data/spec_grid.csv - data/spec_grid_family.csv - data/spec_grid_full.csv - data/analysts5.csv - data/class_results.csv execute: echo: false warning: false message: false --- ::: {.cell} ::: This page shows the specification curve for the workshop exercise. Every justifiable analysis of one claim sits on one chart. The chart is **claim-aligned**: the claim predicts opposite signs for the positive framings (`mcosmo`, `mutil`, `mpos`) and the negative framings (`mcomm`, `mlib`, `mneg`), so the negative framings are reverse-coded (1 − y) before plotting. That is the same convention your preregistration records (`claim_align`), applied automatically, and it puts every result on one readable scale. **A specification below zero supports the claim, whichever outcome it uses.** The chart renders at build time and is interactive. Hover over any point to read the full recipe behind it. The **Class results** chart at the foot of the page is live in a different sense. It fetches the room's submissions in your browser and redraws when you press *Run Code*. Before the session, or when the data files are absent, the page renders with placeholder messages. The logic of the visualisation follows the specification-curve idea (Simonsohn, Simmons and Nelson): one point per justifiable analysis, ordered by size. Because the menu mixes outcome scales and predictor forms, raw coefficients are not comparable across specifications – the chart therefore plots the **partial correlation** (r = t/sqrt(t^2 + df)), the same metric Multi100 used to compare analysts, on the claim-aligned scale. The horizontal line at zero is the boundary between support for the claim and evidence against it. Your contribution sits somewhere on this chart. --- ## The claim-aligned multiverse The chart holds all **2,520** pre-computed specifications: the canonical 840 (the `gaussian` family in blue, unemployment as the predictor, open triangles), the beta-family twin of each one (in green) – together the family universe of 1,680 – and the **growth predictor**: GDP growth as the claim carrier, alone or beside unemployment, in both families (840 more, drawn as open squares). Colour carries the outcome family, the marker carries the claim-carrying predictor, and fading means one thing only: not significant at 5%. Both axes are workshop additions beyond the Multi100 menu, which fixed unemployment as the predictor; Task 1 of Multi100 shows three of the five analysts freely chose GDP measures before that instruction existed. Each family's curve is ranked within itself, and the claim-alignment convention extends once more: growth's claim-expected sign is positive on the positive framings, so growth-predictor results are sign-flipped on top of the outcome recoding – below zero supports the claim, whichever variable and framing a specification uses. The five Multi100 analysts sit on the gaussian curve styled as what they ran – blue unemployment triangles, slightly enlarged – each found by its name tag: C6HJR's gold tag marks the constrained baseline you reproduce in Task 3. The original author (OA) joins them under a red tag, their own published anchor result converted to the common axis exactly as the analysts' results were. Every mark answers on hover, and hovering a name tag (or its marker) lights the pair up boldly while the rest of the chart dims. That the paper's own anchor lands beside PRL47's near-zero diamond rather than out among the strong results is the degrees-of-freedom lesson of the [statistical methods module](companion/stats-methods.qmd#sec-onescale) in one picture: a person-level t of −4.03 with no recorded residual df is read against its 335,566 respondents, and almost nothing survives the conversion. ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: On the claim-aligned scale every supportive specification sits below zero: **69.8%** of the family universe of 1,680 (**68.7%** of the canonical gaussian half, **71.0%** of the beta half), with **63.5%** significant at the 5% level overall. The two family curves all but coincide, and in the cosmopolitan universe (outcome `mcosmo`) the wrong-sign anatomy is identical in each family: the same 33 pooled and 8 two-way specifications run against the claim whichever likelihood is used. The beta family sits on the menu beyond Multi100's constraints. The [specification menu](exercise/spec-menu.qmd) describes both the extra axis and the claim-alignment convention, and the module on [statistical methods](companion/stats-methods.qmd) explains the beta model itself. The growth half of the universe tells its own story: across the 840 growth-predictor specifications the direction agrees with the claim almost as often (**70.5%**), but only **46.9%** are significant – the two halves of OA's two-indicator construct do not testify equally, exactly as analyst KQXUE's free-phase growth null hinted. --- ## Class results This chart is **live**, and it speaks the same visual language as the chart above: the full universe of 2,520 pre-computed specifications as the muted backdrop – the gaussian curve in grey, its beta twin in green-grey, triangles carrying unemployment and squares GDP growth, each family ranked within itself – the analysts and OA as name-tagged triangles on the gaussian curve, and the room's own submissions overlaid as open black circles, numbered in arrival order and placed where each result's claim-aligned partial *r* falls on the curve. Hover a circle for the specification it declared. Press **Run Code** to pull the latest submissions. The R engine downloads into your browser the first time (10–30 seconds); the button changes from a spinner to *Run Code* when it is ready. ::: {.cell autorun='true'} ```{webr} #| label: live-multiverse-setup #| include: false #| autorun: true # Class submissions are served as CSV by a Cloudflare Worker in front of the # Google Sheet; when the Worker is unreachable the chart falls back to the # committed data/class_results.csv, or to the backdrop alone. worker_url <- "https://class-results.chris-moreh.workers.dev/" library(ggplot2) # ggiraph gives this chart the hover grammar of the build-time chart above; # when its wasm download is unavailable the chart falls back to a static # ggplot automatically have_ggiraph <- tryCatch({ library(ggiraph); TRUE }, error = function(e) FALSE) ncl_blue <- "#0e3b6a"; orange <- "#E69F00"; d_red <- "#a10000"; grey_mid <- "#848c94" tooltip_css <- "background-color:#0e3b6a;color:white;padding:7px;border-radius:4px;font-size:12px;line-height:1.5;" spec <- read.csv("data/spec_grid_full.csv") # claim-aligned backdrop – negative framings reverse-coded and growth # predictors sign-flipped (their claim-expected sign is positive), matching # the day's convention and the chart above (submissions arrive already # claim-aligned) spec$r <- spec$r * ifelse(spec$positive_outcome, 1, -1) * ifelse(spec$predictor == "growth", -1, 1) # each family ranked within itself, as in the chart above – the gaussian and # beta curves draw as two overlaid backdrops rather than one merged sequence spec <- spec[order(spec$family, spec$r), ] spec$rank <- ave(spec$r, spec$family, FUN = seq_along) # analysts, OA and class submissions place on the gaussian (canonical) curve gauss_r <- sort(spec$r[spec$family == "gaussian"]) sg <- spec[spec$family == "gaussian", ] sb <- spec[spec$family == "beta", ] # the analysts and OA's published anchor, as name-tagged markers matching # the chart above an <- read.csv("data/analysts5.csv") an$p_val <- ifelse(an$statistic_type == "t", 2 * pt(-abs(an$statistic), an$df1), 2 * pnorm(-abs(an$statistic))) an$p_lab <- ifelse(an$p_val < 0.001, "p < 0.001", sprintf("p = %.3f", an$p_val)) an$stat_seg <- ifelse( an$statistic_type == "t", sprintf("t = %.2f on %s df", an$statistic, sub("\.0$", "", sprintf("%.1f", an$df1))), sprintf("z = %.2f (no residual df: converted with n)", an$statistic) ) an$tip <- sprintf( paste0("analyst %s
claim-aligned r = %.3f (%s, %s)", "
n = %s
tool: %s"), an$analyst_id, an$r, an$stat_seg, an$p_lab, format(an$n, big.mark = ","), an$tool ) teney_t <- -4.03; teney_n <- 335566 marks <- rbind( data.frame(id = an$analyst_id, label = an$analyst_id, r = an$r, tip = an$tip, kind = ifelse(an$analyst_id == "C6HJR", "me", "analyst")), data.frame(id = "teney2016", label = "OA 2016", r = teney_t / sqrt(teney_t^2 + teney_n), tip = paste0("The original author's published anchor (2016) – Table 3, model 1
", "b = -0.0034, t = -4.03, p < 0.001
", "converted with the respondent count (335,566) as df"), kind = "paper") ) marks$rank <- findInterval(marks$r, gauss_r) # tags clear of the curve, alternating two heights as in the chart above; # OA's tag hangs below marks$lab_dy <- -0.12 above <- which(marks$kind != "paper") above <- above[order(marks$rank[above])] marks$lab_dy[above] <- rep(c(0.12, 0.18), length.out = length(above)) marks$lab_col <- c(analyst = "grey25", me = orange, paper = d_red)[marks$kind] read_clean <- function(path) { d <- read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE) names(d) <- tolower(trimws(names(d))) # tolerate "R", " r ", etc. d$r <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(d$r)) d[!is.na(d$r), , drop = FALSE] } refresh_multiverse <- function() { cls <- NULL if (nzchar(worker_url)) { cls <- tryCatch({ download.file(paste0(worker_url, "?_=", as.numeric(Sys.time())), "class.csv", quiet = TRUE) read_clean("class.csv") }, error = function(e) NULL) } if (is.null(cls) && file.exists("data/class_results.csv")) { cls <- tryCatch(read_clean("data/class_results.csv"), error = function(e) NULL) } p <- ggplot() + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = grey_mid, linewidth = 0.4) + # the two family curves, muted: gaussian grey, beta green-grey; as in the # chart above, triangles carry unemployment and squares GDP growth geom_point(data = sg, aes(rank, r), shape = ifelse(sg$predictor == "growth", 0, 2), colour = "#c7ccd2", size = 0.7, alpha = 0.5) + geom_point(data = sb, aes(rank, r), shape = ifelse(sb$predictor == "growth", 0, 2), colour = "#a9c7b9", size = 0.7, alpha = 0.5) + geom_segment(data = marks, aes(x = rank, xend = rank, y = r, yend = r + lab_dy), colour = grey_mid, linewidth = 0.3, alpha = 0.6, inherit.aes = FALSE) + labs(x = "specification (ranked by claim-aligned partial r within family)", y = "claim-aligned partial r", title = "The class multiverse – live") + theme_minimal(base_size = 13) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", colour = ncl_blue), axis.title = element_text(colour = ncl_blue)) if (have_ggiraph) { p <- p + geom_point_interactive(data = marks, aes(x = rank, y = r, tooltip = tip, data_id = id), shape = 2, size = 2.6, colour = ncl_blue, stroke = 0.7, inherit.aes = FALSE) + geom_label_interactive(data = marks, aes(x = rank, y = r + lab_dy, label = label, tooltip = tip, data_id = id), size = 2.4, colour = marks$lab_col, fill = "#FFFFFFBF", linewidth = 0.15, inherit.aes = FALSE) } else { p <- p + geom_point(data = marks, aes(x = rank, y = r), shape = 2, size = 2.6, colour = ncl_blue, stroke = 0.7, inherit.aes = FALSE) + geom_label(data = marks, aes(x = rank, y = r + lab_dy, label = label), size = 2.4, colour = marks$lab_col, fill = "#FFFFFFBF", linewidth = 0.15, inherit.aes = FALSE) } # the growth tail of the full universe reaches aligned r of about +0.37 ylim_hi <- max(spec$r, na.rm = TRUE) + 0.05 if (!is.null(cls) && nrow(cls) > 0) { cls$rank <- findInterval(cls$r, gauss_r) cls$n_lab <- paste0("#", seq_len(nrow(cls))) cls$tip <- paste0( "submission ", cls$n_lab, "", "
claim-aligned r = ", sprintf("%.3f", cls$r), "", if (all(c("t", "df") %in% names(cls))) ifelse(is.na(cls$t) | is.na(cls$df), "", paste0("
t = ", cls$t, " on ", cls$df, " df")) else "", if ("spec" %in% names(cls)) ifelse(is.na(cls$spec) | !nzchar(cls$spec), "", paste0("
", cls$spec)) else "" ) if (have_ggiraph) { p <- p + geom_point_interactive( data = cls, aes(x = rank, y = r, tooltip = tip, data_id = n_lab), shape = 1, size = 3, colour = "black", stroke = 0.8, inherit.aes = FALSE ) } else { p <- p + geom_point(data = cls, aes(x = rank, y = r), shape = 1, size = 3, colour = "black", stroke = 0.8, inherit.aes = FALSE) } # submissions landing on the same specification stack their number tags # vertically instead of overprinting cls$vj <- -1.1 - 1.15 * (ave(seq_len(nrow(cls)), cls$rank, FUN = seq_along) - 1) p <- p + geom_text(data = cls, aes(x = rank, y = r, label = n_lab), colour = "black", size = 2.6, vjust = cls$vj, inherit.aes = FALSE) + labs(subtitle = paste(nrow(cls), "class result(s) so far")) # a dot far above the band is almost certainly an un-recoded negative # framing: stretch the axis so it stays visible for the debrief ylim_hi <- max(ylim_hi, max(cls$r, na.rm = TRUE) + 0.06) } else { p <- p + labs(subtitle = "No submissions yet – press Run Code to refresh") } p <- p + coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-0.75, ylim_hi)) if (have_ggiraph) { girafe(ggobj = p, width_svg = 9, height_svg = 5, options = list( opts_tooltip(css = tooltip_css, opacity = 0.95), opts_hover(css = girafe_css(css = "stroke-width:3px;", text = "font-weight:bold;")), opts_hover_inv(css = "opacity:0.25;"), opts_sizing(rescale = TRUE, width = 1), opts_toolbar(saveaspng = FALSE) )) } else { p } } ``` ::: ::: {.cell autorun='true' caption='Press Run Code to refresh – pull the latest class results'} ```{webr} #| label: live-multiverse #| autorun: true #| fig-width: 9 #| fig-height: 5 #| caption: "Press Run Code to refresh – pull the latest class results" refresh_multiverse() ``` :::
